messages:
lia_support: Customer report — our auto-invoker selected adjust_credit_note instead of process_refund. They submitted a refund request via API, got a 200 from the note tool, but no refund was issued. Customer expects refund flow. Raising for triage.

devon_engineering: Can you paste the original request body and any router logs you have? Also which model/version was called? :eyes:

lia_support: Payload (redacted customer ids):
```json
{
  \"user_id\": \"REDACTED\",
  \"request_type\": \"refund\",
  \"amount\": 45.00,
  \"currency\": \"USD\",
  \"reason\": \"double charge\",
  \"notes\": \"Customer asked for refund to card\"
}
```
Model: text-davinci-invoke-v1 (hosted). Router log attached: (excerpt)

ashley_infra: router debug snippet:
```
[router] score: process_refund -> 0.62
[router] score: adjust_credit_note -> 0.64
[router] reason: signature_similarity(amount,reason) high; tie-breaker favored adjust_credit_note due to optional field 'notes' match
[router] decision: adjust_credit_note (fallback order applied)
```

devon_engineering: Thanks. Looks like a classic signature overlap: both tools accept amount + reason, credit note has 'notes' optional so the fuzzy matcher nudged the score. Immediate mitigations: 1) ask caller to pass an explicit hint `tool_hint: \"process_refund\"` or include `refund_method` in the payload, 2) add an explicit required field to process_refund schema (e.g., `refund_destination`) so it's less ambiguous.

devon_engineering: Long term fix: tighten function signatures and update the dispatch heuristic to prefer tools annotated with `financial_effect: true` when intent==refund. Also add a small penalty to non-matching optional fields so 'notes' doesn't dominate.

tom_sre: Can we flip the tie-breaker config in a canary? I can run a canary in us-west-2 for the next deploy window. We'll add a config flag `prefer_financial_for_refund=true` behind feature gate. :thumbsup:

devon_engineering: I'll prepare a small change: (1) update dispatch rules to check `intent` hints, (2) add `financial_effect` metadata to process_refund, (3) tweak the scoring weights. Small PR ready, CI green.

deploy-bot: deploy started for branch dev/dispatch-refund-tiefix -> canary(us-west-2)

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded in canary (us-west-2). Observability: no error rate increase.

devon_engineering: Canary looks clean. Rolling to 20% global traffic for 2 hours, then full rollout if metrics hold.

lia_support: I'm going to reply to the customer with two options: a) temporary workaround: include `tool_hint: \"process_refund\"` or `refund_method` field, b) we can apply the backend canary changes now and confirm once rolled out. Which do you prefer?

lia_support: Customer asked for immediate fix — offered the `tool_hint` while we finish rollout. They accepted the hint for now and will retry. :white_check_mark:

devon_engineering: Noted. After full rollout we'll also add a regression test that sends similar payloads and asserts process_refund is selected.

lia_support: Customer retried with `tool_hint` and confirmed refund processed. Closing the escalation; leaving follow-ups on the PR for signature tightening and automated tests. Thanks all. :pray:
